header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Atlas Head of ML), Liam O'Neill (Atlas Platform Eng), Priya Kapoor (Atlas CTO)
summary: POC scoping focused on benchmark planning and harness integration. Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, quality thresholds), workload sizing (QPS, token distribution, streaming vs non-streaming ratios), harness setup (customer scripts, locust/k6 vs Redwood harness), timelines for perf runs and access needs. Agreed next steps to exchange traces, repo access, and schedule first perf runs.
topics: Workload sizing: QPS, tokens per request, concurrency
Benchmark harness: integration of customer scripts, repo access
Load testing tooling and run plans (streaming vs non-streaming)
Timelines and gating criteria for POC
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. We've got Samir, our SE, and then i think we have Maya, Liam and Priya from Atlas, correct?
[00:09] Maya: Yep that's right, thanks.
[00:12] Samir: hi all, quick agenda - success criteria, what your workload looks like, how we plug in the benchmark harness and then plan a first perf run.
[00:20] Liam: Sounds good. For context we've got a user-facing recommender generating short prompts, avg 90 tokens per request, with spikes to 500 tokens for certain flows.
[00:29] Jordan: Nice, can you share p95/p99 latency targets?
[00:32] Priya: We're aiming for p95 under 300ms for the short ones, p99 under 800ms, and cost somewhere reasonably less than our current GPU infra.
[00:41] Maya: Also quality criteria: top-k rerank must match our baseline 95% of the time, and hallucination rate below 2% on our eval set.
[00:51] Samir: ok good signals. For the harness integration, we generally support two modes: Redwood's benchmark harness runs your scripts directly (we support Python scripts, locust, k6 patterns), or you can wrap your existing load generator pointing at our endpoint. We also do streaming and non-streaming tests.
[01:05] Liam: What's the delta between streaming vs non-streaming from the infra side? we care because our client uses SSE for the UI.
[01:11] Samir: streaming keeps a connection open and emits tokens incrementally — latency architecture is different since you measure first-token and token-throughput; batching behavior changes. Non-streaming is end-to-end response time only. For batching and KV cache behavior, streaming often has slightly higher per-token overhead but better perceived latency. Also note our K-V cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash in older notes) helps reduce cost for prefix-heavy workloads.
[01:33] Maya: we mostly care about first-byte/first-token latency and p95 p99. Our UI shows spinner until first token.
[01:38] Jordan: ok so success criteria likely: first-token p95 < 200-300ms for short prompts, end-to-end p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms; cost per 1M tokens to be X (we'll put numbers once we have traces).
[01:50] Liam: On workload sizing — our steady QPS is about 120 rps with 2:1 read to write, burst to 400 rps during peak promotions. Average concurrent connections about 300.
[02:02] Samir: perfect, that's actionable. For the harness we'll need the token distribution (histogram) and a small sample of recent production traces (headers, payloads redacted). If you can't share production data we can work with synthetic but it's best to match your distribution.
[02:15] Maya: we can share anonymized traces, there may be compliance steps. We'll coordinate with security.
[02:20] Jordan: on the integration side, Samir can walk through the quickstart: clone the benchmark-harness repo, drop your scripts into /examples, update the workload.json with token histogram, then run ./run_bench — we have a streamed mode flag. We'll send the link.
[02:34] Samir: also a note: if you plan to test private deployment / VPC (Atlas prefers private control plane) we'll need network setup and a short window for SAs to approve. For Dedicated we'll reserve GPU pools for the perf window.
[02:47] Priya: likely we want Dedicated for predictable latency, but want to validate hosted first to compare.
[02:52] Jordan: fair. We'll do hosted perf run as the first step, then Dedicated comparison.
[02:57] Liam: what tooling do you recommend for load generation? we currently use k6 for HTTP and some in-house node scripts.
[03:02] Samir: k6 works fine; our harness has k6 and locust adapters. For streaming tests we have a small node-based harness that opens SSE/Websocket connections and measures first token and continuous throughput; we can drop that into your repo.
[03:17] Maya: great. In terms of metrics, we need p50/p95/p99, server-side token/sec, cost per 1000 tokens, error rates, and end-to-end quality delta on our eval set.
[03:28] Samir: noted. We'll collect per-route breakdowns, token-level cost estimates, tracing hooks. Quick caveat: transcription may swap some names but we'll provide the exact metric names in the README.
[03:39] Jordan: timeline? when can we run the first perf?
[03:42] Liam: security will take 48 hours to approve VPC access, but we can start with anonymized traces and hosted test. If you can send the harness today, we can prep and run by next week.
[03:52] Samir: I can reserve a perf window next Thursday, 10/30. That gives you a week to share traces and scripts.
[03:58] Priya: that works for us. We also want a short gating checklist: functional parity on outputs (quality), latency SLOs, cost comparison, and ops checklist (SSO, audit logs, KMS).
[04:10] Jordan: good gating. On security items, we support SAML/SSO, SOC2, audit logs, and KMS integrations. We'll attach the security pack in the follow-up email.
[04:19] Maya: we will want pointers to the logs and RBAC docs — sometimes the subsystems are different names in notes, e.g., RBAC spelled R-B-A-C in internal docs.
[04:26] Samir: understood. Any blockers on dataset size for the quality eval?
[04:30] Maya: we have ~2k labeled eval prompts for the flows we care about. We'll provide those as a delta test set.
[04:35] Samir: perfect. For benchmarks please include: (1) a short prompt baseline (avg 90 tokens), (2) long prompt path (up to 500 tokens), (3) streaming scenario with UI-first-token measurement. We'll run each scenario with the same seed and measure both throughput and quality regression vs baseline.
[04:50] Liam: for load shape, do you prefer open-loop or closed-loop? our current infra induces closed-loop behavior.
[04:55] Samir: we recommend closed-loop to mimic real production load, but we can run both. Closed-loop will show backpressure effects on latency.
[05:02] Jordan: I'm going to recap actions — send harness + README, Atlas share traces, schedule perf window. Anything else?
[05:08] Priya: include cost modeling template so we can plug in our traffic.
[05:12] Jordan: will do.
[05:15] Maya: one small Q — do you support quantized model variants for Dedicated? we want to check quality vs cost.
[05:21] Samir: yes, we can test quantized variants and include quality regression alerts. We'll capture those in the run. Note quantization names sometimes get mangled in notes (e.g. q8_0 vs q8_1), we'll map exact model IDs in the repo.
[05:33] Liam: ok thanks, that's helpful.
[05:36] Jordan: all right everyone thanks for the time. We'll follow up with the repo link and security pack and book the perf run.
[05:43] Maya: thanks.
[05:44] Priya: thanks all.
[05:45] Samir: bye.
notes: Referenced artifacts: benchmark-harness repo (will share link), security pack (SOC2/KMS/SSO docs), cost model spreadsheet. Customer to provide anonymized traces and eval set. Perf window tentatively 2025-10-30.
